metrics.name: success_rate
metrics.description: Proportion of attempts that yielded a recipe (whether or not the result was already in the inventory). The game tree has ~600 valid recipes from a search space of ~145k pairs; uniform-random pair selection from the full space succeeds at <1%, but with the inventory growing during play a random-combiner empirically reaches ~0.65-0.70 success. Humans (Brändle et al. 2023) hit 0.40-0.50 — *less* than random in raw success terms, because they also explore unfamiliar pairs. Use this metric in conjunction with novelty_rate and unique_pair_rate.

metrics.name: novelty_rate
metrics.description: Proportion of attempts that yielded a novel discovery (a new element added to the inventory). Adults achieve 30-40% novelty rate.

metrics.name: unique_pair_rate
metrics.description: Proportion of attempts whose ordered (a_idx, b_idx) pair has not been tried earlier in the session ('is_unique_pair' is computed by the scorer; pairs are unordered so (a,b) and (b,a) collapse). Humans avoid retrying — Brändle et al. report that adults rarely repeat combinations, with unique-pair rates near 0.95+. A random combiner with growing inventory still repeats pairs as its inventory shrinks vs the explored set.
